pr_comments:
I approve of this but I cannot speak on behalf of the debugger team.

It's unfortunate that the Remote Tree is a completely different thing from the opened Scene display, because code duplication like the one in the PR is required. I considered merging the two someday but it's an very, very daunting task.
This will close https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/2084 and #95209 when merged.

issue_context.title: Remote Scene doesn't use C# IconAttribute for node instanciated, but Inspector is able to use it?
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

Probably reproductible on all version.

### System information

Window 10 - 4.3-RC2

### Issue description

I'm working with Godot C# and I use IconAttribute to have custom icon in the editor. `[GlobalClass, Icon("res://assets/textures/icons/tbd-icon.svg")]` Mostly everywhere you will be able to see the icon, but in the "Remote Scene" the tree view won't show any custom icon for instanciated node. You click on the node which update the Inspector view and you will see the EditorDebuggerRemoteObject do include the CustomIcon but not the Remote Scene 

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/851e8ade-2eb8-4f0d-a1e5-d5c77d8109ef)


### Steps to reproduce

1. This
```csharp
using System;
using Godot;

[GlobalClass, Icon("res://path/to/icon/some-icon.svg")]
public partial class GlobalManager : Node3D, IGlobalManager {
	public static GlobalManager Instance { get; private set; }
}
```
2. Make it Autoload or just instanciate in a working scene. 
3. Run the scene in the debugger and pause (or not!) and look at the Remote Scene tree where custom icon won't be use. 
4. For reference, I use this site (https://uxwing.com/) for icons, and edit the SVG for better representation of the icon. 

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mrp-custom-icon.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16514272/mrp-custom-icon.zip)
comments:
Hello, and thank you for the report.

I'd be curious to know if this is specific to C#, or if it is the same behaviour in GDScript / other languages.

> I'd be curious to know if this is specific to C#, or if it is the same behaviour in GDScript / other languages.

Looks to be the same for gdscript too.

[customicon.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16515901/customicon.zip)

review_comments:
In 4.2.1, this property is still marked as experimental, and I don't think this has changed in 4.3

Maybe it's time to reconsider?

According to the documentation it's specifically the fit modes that are experimental:
> Using EXPAND_FIT_WIDTH, EXPAND_FIT_WIDTH_PROPORTIONAL, EXPAND_FIT_HEIGHT or EXPAND_FIT_HEIGHT_PROPORTIONAL may result in unstable behavior in some containers

Though the property itself is marked experimental it is used in several places in the editor
